name: ZAP
what: An open-source web application security scanner and proxy. It can spider a site, scan passively and actively, and run as a baseline scan in Docker.
when: To test your own web apps in a test or staging environment, and to add a passive baseline scan to CI/CD.
example: Start with the passive baseline scan in Docker: `docker run -t ghcr.io/zaproxy/zaproxy:stable zap-baseline.py -t https://staging.contoso.com`.
To save a report, mount a working folder and add `-r report.html`, as shown in the baseline scan docs.
Triage the warnings, and mark false positives in a config file so later runs stay quiet.
Run active scans only against test environments you are allowed to attack.
pitfalls: Active scans submit forms and can create data or trigger emails; avoid production.
Authenticated areas need a login configuration, or ZAP only sees the public pages.
The baseline scan is passive and will not find every issue.
